a female given name
to pose, to lodge
figuratively
transitive
Die Beklagte stellte den Antrag, die Klage abzuweisen.
The defendant lodged the application to reject the claim.
Kann ich dir eine Frage stellen?
Can I ask you a question?
to provide, to afford, to place at someone's disposal
transitive
Die Schutzbekleidung muss vom Arbeitgeber gestellt werden.
The protective gear must be provided by the employer.
Aus dem Sicherungsvertrage war die A-Gesellschaft verpflichtet, eine Bürgschaft zu stellen.
From the surety agreement the A company was obliged to provide a suretyship.
to encounter and stop, to intercept
transitive
Die Hunde haben den Hirsch gestellt.
The hounds stopped the stag.
Die Polizei stellte den Dieb.
The police stopped (and arrested) the thief.
to set, adjust
transitive
Müssen wir am Sonntag wieder die Uhren stellen?
Do we have to adjust the clocks again on Sunday?
to expose oneself to, to succumb to, to come out to face, to confront
reflexive
Du musst dich der Gefahr stellen.
You have to face the danger.
Der Dieb stellte sich der Polizei.
The thief surrendered to the police.
to feign, to simulate, to pretend
transitive
Es war alles nur gestellt!
It was all fake!
Sie hatte ihre Krankheit nur gestellt.
She merely simulated her ailment.

stellen.et: From Middle High German stellen, from Old High German stellen, from Proto-West Germanic *stalljan (“to put, position”), from Proto-Indo-European *stel- (“to place, put, post, stand”).

s: stilt
Der Clown geht auf Stelzen.
The clown walks on stilts.
wagtail (genus Motacilla)
Die Bachstelze gehört zu den Stelzen.
The white wagtail is a wagtail.
pork knuckle
Austria
Stelze.et: From Middle High German stelze, from Old High German stelza, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *staltijǭ, which is related to *stalljan (“to place, put”). Cognate with Middle Low German stelte, Dutch stelt, English stilt.

s: location, spot (specific location in space, relevant in context but typically otherwise unmarked)
Ich versuche die Stelle wiederzufinden, wo wir uns das erste Mal getroffen haben.
I'm trying to find the spot where we met for the first time.
spot (specific location on skin or another surface, often featuring damage or a different property)
Hier am Knie ist eine Stelle, wo die Hose schon gerissen ist.
Here, at the knee, there's a spot where the pants are already torn.
spot, part, bit (brief section of a book, movie, piece of music, etc., typically encompassing a few seconds or lines at most)
Die Stelle in dem Stück gefällt mir besonders.
This part of the piece is one I like in particular.
point (situation or status reached by a certain amount of progress through an endeavor)
Dann hat es auch noch angefangen zu regnen, und an der Stelle mussten wir die Wanderung abbrechen.
Then, on top of this, it also started to rain, and we had to abort the hike at that point.
place, position (position within a certain ordering or ranking)
Das Land kommt in dieser Statistik erst an zehnter Stelle.
The country comes in at tenth place in this statistic.
position specifically in terms of importance (both of opinions and objective evaluations of influence)
Vertrauen steht bei uns an erster Stelle.
Trust is the most important thing to us.
synonym of Dezimalstelle
position, job (set of tasks or responsibilities meant to be filled by the employment of one person)
sich um/auf eine Stelle bewerben
to apply for a position
department, office (organizational unit bearing the responsibility for a specific task, particularly in the public sector)
position, posture (specific way of holding or positioning the body)
sex position
position (position attained against the competition of others, but not numerically quantified)
Die Firma nutzt ihre Stellung als Marktführer aus.
The company takes advantage of its position as market leader.
Der Zerfall des Römerreiches raubte der Stadt Rom die alte Stellung als Mittelpunkt alles Geschehens.
The decay of the Roman empire robbed the city of Rome of the old position as the center of all that was happening.
position (defended spot to be held and from where to prepare attacks)
stance, position, opinion (expressed view regarding a matter of discussion)
zu etwas Stellung nehmen
to state one's opinion on something, to (officially) comment something
medical examination

proxy, representative, agent
proxy, substitute, surrogate
proxy pattern
Stellvertreter.et: 17th century, from Stelle (“place”) + vertreten (“to represent, fill in”) + -er (“-er”), probably after French lieutenant, Latin locum tenēns.
